title: Creating qualitative datasets in geoarchaeology: An easy-applicable description template for archaeological thin section analysis using Stoops 2003
author: Marcazzan, Meinekat

steps.title: Initial visual inspection and scanning
steps.instruction: Observe the thin section with the naked eye (optionally on a light table), then scan it at low and high resolution using a flatbed scanner and a film scanner.

steps.title: Record general sample information
steps.instruction: Enter basic metadata into the template: site name, sample ID, year, analyst, excavation unit, layer and/or feature. Attach the PPL and XPL scans and write a brief note on naked‑eye observations or field particularities.

steps.title: Microscopic observation under multiple lighting
steps.instruction: Examine the thin section first with a stereomicroscope (low magnification) and then with a petrographic microscope (high magnification). Perform observations in plane‑polarized light (PPL) and crossed‑polarized light (XPL), and optionally use oblique incident light (OIL) and blue‑light fluorescence. Save representative images for each lighting mode.

steps.title: Document each micro‑unit details
steps.instruction: For every micro‑unit present in the thin section, fill out the corresponding sections of the template.

substeps.instruction: Identify the micro‑unit (and, if applicable, the micro‑facies type).
Describe the groundmass and its fabric.
Identify main components, categorising them as geogenic, biogenic or anthropogenic; note any weathering (using the provided check‑boxes).
Describe pedofeatures using the drop‑down term list.
Characterise the interface to the upper unit.

steps.title: Add additional micro‑units if needed
steps.instruction: If the thin section contains more than one micro‑unit, duplicate the micro‑unit rows in the template and repeat the documentation steps for each extra unit.

steps.title: Log supplementary analytical techniques
steps.instruction: At the end of the template, indicate any additional analyses performed on the thin section (e.g., µFTIR, µXRF, SEM) using the check‑boxes or the “Others” field, and add any final notes or literature references.
